svg.title: aF4 trigger protoboard layout
svg.desc: Perfboard cut to ~30x33mm (25x25mm 9x9 grid minimum), component side: AQY212GH PhotoMOS SSR on the isolation boundary, 220 ohm LED resistor and 10k GPIO pulldown standing vertically on the 3.3V side, and the rev C regulator block on the 12V side: LM1117T-ADJ (TO-220, lying flat tab-up) with R4 121R (OUT to ADJ) / R5 887R (ADJ to GND) setting 10.41V, C1 10uF input cap and C2 10uF output cap (both the same 10uF 50V aluminium electrolytic, positive leg to the left in each position). Raw fused 12V enters the board; 10.4V is made on-board. Splitter feeds the DC-099 panel jack, whose pigtails run through the 100mA polyfuse to the board; P6KE15CA bidirectional TVS spliced behind the 3.5mm plug. Detail panels below show the polyfuse splice and the TVS splice at the plug.
svg.text: aF4 trigger — protoboard layout (component side, rev C)

g.text: ① +12V: splitter → DC-099 panel jack → 100 mA
② P6KE15CA TVS spliced ~1" behind plug: tip↔sleeve, no polarity
Regulator is ON the board — no buck module, nothing to pre-set

svg.text: TO-220 flat, tab up · 24 mW · no heatsink

g.text: · Board: cut ~30 × 33 mm (25 × 25 mm / 9×9 grid min).
· Mount: drill the 4 dashed holes to Ø2.2 mm — they
are 6 pitches (15.24 mm) apart, matching the case
· R1/R2 stand vertically (bend at the shoulder, sleeve
the bent lead, land both in the GPIO13 hole). R4
stands the same way; R5 lies flat or stands.
· Meter R4/R5 before soldering — swapped, the rail
reads ~1.4 V and the feed never triggers.
· C1 = C2 = one part (10µF 50V electrolytic), both polarized:
+ leg left (C1 → IN, C2 → 10.4V rail), − leg to 12V−.
· U2 PADS top→bottom: IN, ADJ, OUT. U2 PINS are 1=ADJ,
2=OUT(tab), 3=IN — so the leads fan out of line and
pin 1 CROSSES pin 2. Sleeve pin 1's lead.
A bare crossing shorts ADJ↔OUT → raw 12V on the tip.
· SSR notch faces R1 · SLEEVE to 12V− only, never ESP32 GND.
Off-board detail (rev C) — splice these, then wire to the board (nothing to pre-set)
① 100 mA polyfuse (MF-R010), inline on the DC-099 jack's +12V pigtail

Splitter's male plug clicks into the jack from outside — nothing gets cut. PTC has no polarity; radial discs have both legs on one edge, so bend one 180° to exit the far side. Steady draw ~15 mA, so the 100 mA hold gives real fault margin.
② P6KE15CA TVS (bidirectional), spliced ~1" behind the 3.5 mm plug
either leg either way — no polarity
DO-15 axial: wrap a leg around each conductor
SLEEVE ties to the 12V− strip only — never to ESP32 GND. 12.8 V standoff sits above the 10.4 V line — zero standing leakage into the port.
